item.title: City of Lawrence will remove Watson Park basketball court, prone to flooding, this summer
item.description: The city plans to remove the basketball court in Watson Park, which is prone to flooding, during the summer as part of ongoing construction, and it's not yet clear whether a new court will replace it. Continue reading ...

item.title: End of construction on Iowa Street is in sight; road to fully reopen next week
item.description: Lawrence motorists may have noticed four open lanes on Iowa Street Thursday after almost a year of construction work. There are still a few finishing touches to be made, but the city will fully open the street next week. Continue reading ...

item.title: Lawrence school district para had unlawful relationship with student, court documents allege
item.description: A former paraeducator in the Lawrence school district carried out an inappropriate relationship with a middle schooler, and in one instance touched the student against his will, court documents allege. Continue reading ...

item.title: Lawrence-Douglas County Public Health launches new board for suicide prevention
item.description: Lawrence-Douglas County Public Health has implemented a new private board that reviews local suicides to inform prevention strategies. Continue reading ...

item.title: Tennessee Street to reopen in Old West Lawrence; Iowa Street to get finishing touches
item.description: Although some major construction projects in Lawrence are ongoing and will be for months to come, two key streets are close to reopening. Continue reading ...

item.title: Lawrence school board to meet for midyear evaluation of superintendent
item.description: The Lawrence school board has called a special meeting to complete a midyear evaluation of Superintendent Jeanice Swift. Continue reading ...

item.title: Prairie Band Potawatomi intends to ditch $30M ICE contract, chairman announces
item.description: The Prairie Band Potawatomi Tribe’s chairman compared immigrant detention to Indian reservations in an online video address Friday, and declared the tribe’s intention to jettison a recently secured contract to design detention centers. Continue reading ...

item.title: Johnson County officers kill a stabbing suspect at Panasonic plant. Here’s what we know
item.description: The Panasonic plant in De Soto shut down after officers shot a person suspected of stabbing another. The suspect is dead, and the stabbing victim was transported to the hospital in critical condition. Continue reading ...

item.title: Lawrence advisory boards will reevaluate city’s goal to achieve fully renewable energy usage
item.description: Members of two Lawrence advisory boards will soon put their heads together to evaluate whether the city’s renewable energy goals are realistic, and how they line up with overarching sustainability plans for the county. Continue reading ...
